cards.q: What are the six VPN technologies compared for ENCOR?
cards.a: GRE (transport/multicast), IPsec (encryption), DMVPN (dynamic spokes), FlexVPN (unified IKEv2 framework), GET VPN (tunnel-free any-to-any over MPLS), and SSL VPN (remote user access).

cards.q: What is the key difference between GRE and IPsec?
cards.a: GRE provides no encryption but carries multicast and any routing protocol over a tunnel, while IPsec provides encryption but does not directly carry multicast or routing; the classic combination is GRE-in-IPsec.

cards.q: How do DMVPN and FlexVPN differ?
cards.a: DMVPN uses mGRE and NHRP for dynamic spoke-to-spoke tunnels and may run IKEv1 or IKEv2, while FlexVPN is IKEv2-only and uses IKEv2 profiles, supporting site-to-site, remote access, and hub-spoke.

cards.q: What makes GET VPN different from DMVPN and crypto-map IPsec?
cards.a: GET VPN has no tunnel interfaces and uses a shared GDOI group key for direct any-to-any encryption, whereas DMVPN and crypto-map/VTI build point-to-point tunnels.

cards.q: What is the advantage of SSL VPN over IPsec remote access?
cards.a: SSL VPN uses TLS/DTLS on ports 443, which passes most NAT and firewalls with low setup friction, while IPsec remote access uses UDP 500/4500 which is sometimes blocked and requires an IPsec client.

cards.q: Which VPN technology would you choose to carry multicast plus routing protocols?
cards.a: GRE over IPsec, because GRE supports multicast and any IGP/BGP over the tunnel while IPsec provides the encryption.

cards.q: Which VPN technology is best for dynamic branches over the Internet without a hub bottleneck?
cards.a: DMVPN, because mGRE plus NHRP lets spokes build direct IPsec tunnels to each other after registering at the hub.

cards.q: Which VPN technology provides tunnel-free any-to-any encryption over an MPLS backbone?
cards.a: GET VPN, which uses a GDOI group key so routers encrypt directly to each other with no tunnel interfaces or overlay routing.

cards.q: A company wants one framework covering both site-to-site tunnels and remote access clients; which technology fits?
cards.a: FlexVPN, because it is an IKEv2 profile-based framework that supports site-to-site, remote access, hub-and-spoke, and spoke-to-spoke configurations.

cards.q: Which commands help compare and verify the VPN technologies?
cards.a: show dmvpn, show crypto session, show crypto ipsec sa, show ip nhrp, show vpn-sessiondb, and show ip mroute to inspect group/tunnel state.

cards.q: What is a common VPN exam misconception about GRE?
cards.a: That GRE alone provides security; GRE does not encrypt at all and must be paired with IPsec for confidentiality.

cards.q: What is the VPN technology quick-review summary?
cards.a: Pick IPsec for encrypting fixed links, GRE over IPsec when you need multicast and routing, DMVPN for dynamic Internet branches, FlexVPN for a unified IKEv2 framework, GET VPN for tunnel-free any-to-any on MPLS, and SSL VPN for remote users.
